sections.html:
Selling here means choosing among a broker, a sale you run yourself, or a buyer paying cash who takes on the repairs. Every route finishes at one Cuyahoga County desk for transfer and recording, which leaves time and renovation effort as the real question. Landlords also owe the city a rental certificate on rented single, double and triple homes.

  • Pick a broker if the house is in good shape and you can live with tours and an inspection report.
  • Skipping the agent saves commission, but the contract and deed work lands on you and whoever handles closing.
  • Cash suits estate houses, long-deferred repairs, empty rentals and tight moving dates.

North Royalton is a suburb in southern Cuyahoga County covering 21.32 square miles, with 31,322 residents at the 2020 census. The mid-2025 estimate is 30,936. Growth has been slow, from 30,444 in 2010, so a listing here mostly competes with other established houses. Owners occupy about seven in ten homes, and more than nine in ten residents stayed put the year before.

sections.h2: Rental certificate and short-term rental limits
sections.html:
For a rented house, Chapter 1485 of the city ordinances calls for a Certificate of Rental Registration from the Building Commissioner before anyone moves in. File it by December 31 ahead of the year it covers, or within thirty days of the house first turning into a rental. It ends on December 31 of its year. Multi-unit owners must renew every year or file an exemption form.

Timing sets the fee. A single-family rental registered by February 1 pays $50, and one filed after March 1 pays $125. An exemption form costs nothing before February 1 and $50 afterward. Skipping registration is a first-degree misdemeanor under the chapter.

Nightly rentals are tightly limited. The chapter treats any stay under thirty consecutive days as short-term. Tenant-occupied units cannot host transient guests at all. Owner-occupants may host for at most fourteen days a year, must live in the home at least 351 days a year, and need a transient rental registration certificate. A buyer who counted on nightly rental income needs to hear this before bidding.

State law adds one more step on a rental sale: the county stamps the deed with a reminder that the incoming owner files owner information with the auditor under Ohio Revised Code 5323.02.

sections.h2: How a sale is recorded in Cuyahoga County
sections.html:
Transfers go through the county Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division, which absorbed the earlier auditor, recorder and engineer offices. Real Estate Services requires one of two forms with every transfer: DTE 100, the value statement and receipt, or DTE 100-EX, which explains why no conveyance fee is owed.

Ohio Senate Bill 94 set the current recording fee on October 24, 2024: $39 covers two pages and every extra page is $8. Find the division on the fourth floor at 2079 E. Ninth Street in Cleveland. Weekday recording stops at 4 p.m. Staff may not offer legal advice, and drafting a deed counts as practicing law, so let a closing agent or lawyer prepare it.

Under section 5302.30 of the Ohio code, sellers hand buyers a property disclosure form promptly. Estate fiduciary transfers are among the exemptions.

Inherited houses take special routes at the county. The conveyance standards describe an affidavit of real estate inherited under Ohio Revised Code 317.22, a probate court certificate of transfer, and a survivorship affidavit under 5302.17. A separate Great Estates Program page is aimed at families settling an estate.

The right paper depends on how title passed to you. Ask the probate court or your closing agent which one applies before you sign a contract. Once that document is recorded, the sale moves through the same steps as any other: contract, title work, deed, DTE form, recording.

sections.h2: From signed contract to recorded deed
sections.html: The order of events is the same whichever route you pick. First the contract is signed and title work begins. If the house was a rental, the rental certificate and any county owner filing get sorted out. Next the disclosure form goes to the buyer, unless an exemption such as an estate fiduciary transfer applies. Then your closing agent or lawyer drafts the deed and fills in DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX. At closing the settlement agent divides the tax bill and pays off anything owed. Last, the deed and form go to the Fiscal Officer's division on East Ninth Street with the recording fee. Ask for a copy of each document so your own file is complete.

sections.h2: Tax bills and the Board of Revision
sections.html:
County real estate bills run a year behind, so what is payable in one calendar year covers the year before. Each bill is split into two halves, and an unpaid half picks up a 10 percent penalty. Phone the County Treasurer for this year's due dates instead of trusting an old calendar.

The settlement agent divides the current bill between you and the buyer and takes any past-due amount from your proceeds, so find out early what you owe. A value that seems too high can be challenged with the county Board of Revision, which accepts complaints yearly through March 31. A closing statement or DTE 100 counts as evidence. The board can also raise a value, so file only with solid numbers.

sections.h2: Is a cash buyer worth a call?
sections.html:
Usually the answer turns on time and condition. Cash buyers purchase as is, which removes contractors, showings and appraisal waits. That can help when an estate must wrap up, a rental has tenant trouble or a move has a firm date.

Insist on a written offer and measure it against a listing's take-home after commission and repairs. Settle who covers the recording fee, what the closing date is, and who deals with the rental certificate and the county owner filing if tenants lived there. Title work, the deed and the DTE form still apply to a cash sale, and a house with open rental paperwork needs that cleared first.

faqs.q: Does a rented North Royalton house need a certificate?
faqs.a: Yes, if the house is a rental. Chapter 1485 bars anyone from occupying a residential rental unit unless a current Certificate of Rental Registration has been issued, and the certificate expires each December 31. Keep it current while tenants live there.

faqs.q: Where is a North Royalton deed filed?
faqs.a: At the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division, with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX attached. Recording costs $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page beyond that.

faqs.q: Are nightly rentals allowed in North Royalton?
faqs.a: Only in narrow cases. Owners living in the home 351 or more days a year may host guests up to fourteen days annually with a registration certificate. Tenant-occupied units may not host them.

faqs.q: What is the penalty on a late Cuyahoga County tax bill?
faqs.a: Ten percent is added to an unpaid half-year bill. Ask the Treasurer for the due dates that apply this year.

faqs.q: What if I inherited the North Royalton house?
faqs.a: Title reaches the heirs through a probate court certificate or an affidavit of real estate inherited, and the county lists both routes in its conveyance standards. An heir who did not live in the house within the past year is generally excused from the Ohio disclosure form, but should confirm with a closing agent.
